title: Choose TAHANIVO's visual world
question: Choose the identity world that should guide the logo and furniture storefront, or re-roll the set.

options.label: Cobalt Lacquer Pavilion
options.lineage: color-field interiors and lacquered architectural screens
options.thesis: Exclusive furniture is staged as sculpture inside a saturated cobalt pavilion.
options.viewport: A cobalt room fills the screen while one sculptural chair and a flat two-plane aperture mark hold the composition.
options.risk: The color must frame the furniture without making the store feel like an art installation first.

raised.raise: The catalog grid now locks to measured modules so expressive color never weakens shopping clarity.

options.label: The Material Library
options.lineage: architect material archives and cabinetmaker sample walls
options.thesis: Luxury is proven through materials, joinery, and finish instead of being claimed.
options.viewport: A measured sample wall surrounds one hero product and an interlocking abstract joint mark.
options.risk: This is the most naturally credible direction, but also the closest to familiar architecture branding.

options.label: The Living Alcove
options.lineage: asymmetric spatial composition and active negative space
options.thesis: Each piece is given one quiet room, with balance and emptiness doing the selling.
options.viewport: A single chair sits low in an off-center plaster alcove beside a three-stroke balance mark.
options.case: Product clarity is excellent, but the cultural coding is less truthful for a brand with no stated geographic origin.
options.risk: It can imply a Japanese provenance that TAHANIVO does not claim.

options.label: Living Surface Portal
options.lineage: full-bleed digital material and responsive light
options.thesis: The storefront behaves like a living material around sharply photographed furniture.
options.viewport: A minimal aperture logo and one chair float over a slowly shifting deep-blue material field.
options.case: It strongly signals exclusivity, but the digital atmosphere can compete with furniture evaluation.
options.risk: Performance and product legibility require strict restraint.

options.label: Cobalt Tile Gallery
options.lineage: modular tile halls and framed narrative panels
options.thesis: Collections unfold as cobalt rooms built from whole measured modules.
options.viewport: A tiled blue-and-white gallery frames furniture inside a modular abstract tile mark.
options.case: Fuses poorly because pattern dominates the furniture and suggests a regional story the brand does not hold.
options.risk: The surface can become decorative before it becomes luxurious.

canonCard.label: Luxury Furniture Editorial
canonCard.thesis: The familiar premium furniture catalog, executed with restraint and excellent photography.
canonCard.viewport: A spacious cream hero pairs a large room photograph with a refined abstract furniture-plane mark.
canonCard.risk: Beautiful and clear, but intentionally difficult to distinguish from established furniture brands.
